1 نَهَتَ , aor.
نَهِتَ , [cont? to analogy,] inf. n. نَهِيتٌ (S, K) and نُهَاتٌ (K) He cried out, or uttered a cry: (TA:) [see إِنْهَتِى عَلَيْهَا voce بَهَتَ:] he uttered the kind of sound termed زَئِير; [i. e., he (a lion, TA) uttered a sound from his chest; or roared:] (K:) or he uttered a sound lower than that which is termed زئير: (S:) or he breathed hard; or emitted the voice, or the breath, with a moaning; i. q. زَحَرَ, (K,) and طَحَرَ: (TA:) or he uttered a sound from his chest on an occasion of distress. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
